timeline.text: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity
Chest x-ray: pulmonary vascular congestion, small bilateral effusions

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 58-year-old female admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.65, bnp 1408, creatinine 0.86, hemoglobin 13, platelets 283, sodium 140, wbc 9; vitals dbp 69-73, heart_rate 83-86, map 85-89, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 116-122, spo2 96-98, temp 36.6-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: pulmonary vascular congestion, small bilateral effusions; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Furosemide 40 mg IV; Transthoracic echo: LVEF 34%, global hypokinesis
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Acute HFrEF exacerbation.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.84, hemoglobin 12.8, platelets 283, sodium 139, wbc 8.9; vitals dbp 69-73, heart_rate 83-89, map 86-88, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 117-120, spo2 96-98, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Furosemide 40 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Acute HFrEF exacerbation. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 58-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Acute HFrEF exacerbation. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
